name: evtx_query
description: Query an EVTX event log and return filtered events with timestamp, event id, channel, computer, provider, EventRecordID and named data fields. A run reports three counts apart: records_examined (every record the reader produced), events_matched (records that parsed and passed every filter) and parse_errors (records or chunk chains that could not be read, with their offsets); an error row is never counted as a match, and a run with any parse error, or whose chunks could not be enumerated to the end, is status partial. Every answer and refusal carries status and status_basis. Every row carries record_offset, chunk_offset, the EventRecordID and record_filetime (the FILETIME in the record header, as a decimal string, with record_time_utc by integer arithmetic) beside the XML's own SystemTime. Filters: event_ids, contains (a substring of the XML), start_record and end_record, and start_time and end_time (ISO 8601: YYYY-MM-DD then optionally THH, THH:MM, THH:MM:SS or THH:MM:SS.fffffff, and from the hour on Z or an offset such as +03:00; no zone is UTC; a time names the span its precision gives, so a date is the whole day; the SystemTime of each record is converted to UTC ticks and compared as a number; a malformed time, a word such as yesterday, or a range that ends before it starts is refused; a record with no SystemTime is left out of a time range and counted in events_without_time_excluded, and the run is partial). The log is accounted for as a whole: chunks_declared (what the file header says), chunks_read (what the reader gave), bytes_expected and file_bytes; a file shorter than its header says or a reader that gave fewer chunks than declared is status partial with a problem naming both, not a log with no records. The file is read to its end, not to the header's count: a chunk past the declared count that has an ElfChnk signature and passes the chunk-header checks is read (its rows say chunk_beyond_declared: true; chunks_in_file, chunks_read_beyond_declared, header_flags and header_dirty say what the file holds), one that has the signature and fails the checks is a problem, an all-zero slot past the count is free space; a declared chunk with no signature is named and not read. A chunk whose string or template table loops or points outside the chunk is not given to python-evtx (which follows them without end): it is named under chunks_not_read, and whatever else the library does is read under a timer of 8 seconds per chunk, after which the chunk is given up and named; the whole run stops at its own time limit (57 seconds) with status partial, and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON (status interrupted, exit 128 plus the signal) and a partial_result_file that is named as a partial and is not a result. A file that does not begin with ElfFile, a path that is not a regular file, and an out_file that is not text are refused as JSON. The XML of every match is kept in the result file (JSON Lines), which is mode 0600, is written under a temporary name and placed at the end, and never replaces or truncates an earlier result: a result of the same bytes is named again, and when the name is held by another file the first free -2, -3... beside it is used and result_file_requested says so; its default name is made from the arguments without `contains`, so a needle never reaches a file name. limit is the inline page size. SENSITIVE: event data can hold command lines and text typed into one, which can hold a secret; run it as a job with secret_output: true when the log may.

event_ids.description: Optional list of numeric event IDs to include

contains.description: Optional case-insensitive substring that must appear in the XML

limit.description: Events shown inline (default 200, an inline page size); every matching event and its whole XML is kept in result_file, and parse-error rows are listed under errors and kept there too

out_file.description: Optional JSONL result path under the run (in a job, under $OUT); defaults to work/<your id>/tool-output/ (in a job, $OUT). An existing file is never replaced: the first free name beside it is used and named

start_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 lower bound on the XML's SystemTime: the beginning of the span the text names (2026-09-01 is 00:00 that day, 2026-09-01T10:00 is 10:00:00); no zone is UTC, Z or an offset is applied

end_time.description: Optional ISO 8601 upper bound on the XML's SystemTime: the end of the span the text names, so 2026-09-01 includes the whole day and 2026-09-01T10:00 that whole minute; no zone is UTC, Z or an offset is applied
